propositions: Python 3.11 Path.rglob caches child directory entries and raises FileNotFoundError when a cached entry vanishes during recursion, whereas Python 3.12+ tolerates this via walk-based iteration.

Session teardown fixture _remove_readonly_run_snapshots traverses tmp_path with rglob, entering unrelated mutable subtrees including the live tracker lock directory that is created and destroyed by canonical store write operations.

Monkeypatching os.name to 'nt' during test execution causes pathlib.Path() factory calls in conftest.py and snapshot.py to select WindowsPath on Python 3.11, raising NotImplementedError on POSIX systems when invoked during teardown before monkeypatch restoration.

The fixture must recursively discover and remove exact .rebar/run_snapshots roots while preserving unrelated snapshot content, tolerating only FileNotFoundError for concurrently vanished entries, and propagating all other filesystem errors.

A deterministic barrier using real LockHandle.release() at the parent scandir point reproduces the exact cached-entry FileNotFoundError on Python 3.11 in the actual fixture teardown, while Python 3.12 returns normally under identical interleaving.

Repair requires os.walk with onerror to ignore only FileNotFoundError, scoping concrete Path construction through the test-harness cleanup helpers to match the caller's pathlib flavor, and preserving production _rmtree_writable behavior for non-test callers.
